claim_versions.statement: For p>0, spectral beta>max(0,p-1) yields an exact weighted affine probability law.
For p>0,beta>=0, an exact law gives weighted inverse-area integrability and almost-every-target compact positive superlevels at k=(beta+p+1)/(p+2)>1/2.
Generic regular targets admit a Borel, equivariant, fiberwise-injective, strictly height-increasing saddle-to-maximum rank pairing.
The exact law implies E[J(i)]<=0; equality forces J identically zero almost surely, including fixed-root exceptional targets and nonuniform strict gain.
For k>0, a normalized univalent map has identically zero critical-map Jacobian only when k=1; then it is affine or a unique real-vertex normalized quadratic.
evidence: verify.py zero-J circle and quadratic identities
